sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: International Air Freight Forwarding and Cargo Aircraft Charter

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic code foundation with Germanic customary heritage and EU supra-national supremacy)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg-China Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1979, as amended by the 2014 Protocol)
Luxembourg-Hong Kong SAR Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (2010)
Luxembourg-United States Double Taxation Convention (1996, as amended by the 2004 and 2009 Protocols)
EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) investment chapter (EU-level)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Act of 10 August 1915, as amended, on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), in particular Title IV Part II regarding the SCSp introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013; concordance with Luxembourg Civil Code and RCS organizational rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), entity incorporation department (RCSonline).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Coordinated Articles of Association for a Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp), signed by or on behalf of the General Partner, filed by a Luxembourg incorporated service provider or lawyer through RCSonline.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum or paid-up capital requirement for an SCSp; contribution amount and payment timetable are freely fixed in the partnership agreement. If the partnership agreement provides for an initial contribution to a blocked escrow/bank account, such credit must be evidenced prior to registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the capital contributions of the initial limited partners set out in the proposed partnership agreement are accepted and subscribed for the SCSp's air cargo charter brokerage business (ISIC 5229); FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office be fixed at [Registered Address], Luxembourg, and the general partner is authorized to execute and file the coordinated articles with the Luxembourg Business Registers; FURTHER RESOLVED that [Name] is appointed sole manager of the general partner, with full power to open bank accounts, sign charter and brokerage contracts, file tax and regulatory returns, and perform all administrative acts required for operations; FURTHER RESOLVED that the manager shall obtain all applicable civil aviation, environmental, and occupational clearances.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Articles of Association and Pre-Incorporation Consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized Luxembourg service provider / notary (if public deed elected); no notarization required for private-deed SCSp.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Check and reserve the proposed SCSp name using the RCS extract query; draft the SCSp partnership agreement containing identity of general and limited partners, scope, capital contributions, profit-sharing rules, management powers, and registered office address. Have the general partner(s) and any appointing corporate officer sign the private deed or notarial instrument. Provide the Luxembourg service provider with all due diligence originals and declarations of non-conviction for the manager.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement of the SCSp
Identity documents and proof of registration of general partner entities
Declarations of non-conviction of managers/directors
Memorandum describing the intended activity under ISIC 5229/NAICS 488510
Separate power of attorney for the agent signing the RCS filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected as too similar or misleading, submit three alternative names and re-run the RCS name screening; no penalty if the amendment is completed before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration in the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed coordinated articles, the appointment of the manager, and the registered office consent with RCSonline together with the agent certificate. Pay the filing fee electronically. After verification, the RCS assigns the SCSp registration number and sends the confirmation excerpt. The registration is effective against third parties as of the date of the RCS entry.
required_dossiers: Signed coordinated articles of association
Proof of identity/powers of the general partner and manager
Registered office address consent
Initial beneficial owner declaration sheet
RCS filing fee receipt
Power of attorney authorizing the registered agent to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues an 'avis de supplément' or rejects the filing, the petitioner has one month to submit a corrective deed or additional evidence. If the rejection is nonetheless maintained, a formal appeal may be filed before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within two months of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Coordinated Deed in the Electronic Compendium of Companies and Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RESA publication module.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS automatically transmits the incorporated entities' legal acts to RESA. The publication occurs once the registration certificate is generated. Obtain the RESA publication notice form for third-party evidence. This step is automatic after incorporation in the RCS; no separate user submission is required.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
RESA publication visa generated by the registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication is delayed or contains a clerical defect, send a written request to LBR via the RCSonline module for correction; in the case of a substantive defect, file an amendatory deed and request publication of the corrected version.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, Social Security, and Beneficial Ownership Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Luxembourg Business Registers for RBE.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request a national business registration (NLC) from the RCS which serves as tax ID; then complete the AEDT VAT registration form 640 for potential VAT liability; register with ACD for corporate income and municipal business tax and, if applicable, withholding. From the date of registration the SCSp must declare the UBO(s) to the RBE beneficial owner register within one month. Any expected employment triggers simultaneous CCSS registration.
required_dossiers: RCS incorporation certificate / NLC
SCSp partnership agreement
Authorized signatory list
Statement of activities and expected turnover for VAT
Identity details of beneficial owners for RBE
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where tax or VAT registrations are queried, the taxpayer may file an administrative objection with the relevant director within three months and, failing a response, appeal to the administrative tribunal within three months of the decision. RBE late filing may expose fines, but an immediate voluntary submission and justification letters usually avoid penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Civil Aviation Security and Air Cargo Charter Permits
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direction de l'Aviation Civile (DAC) – Ministry of Mobility and Public Works, Luxembourg.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Since the SCSp will operate solely as an air cargo charter broker and will not be an EU air carrier, apply for an Indirect Air Carrier (IAC) recognition / broker declaration by submitting the company security programme, details of cargo screening arrangements, and the charter broker liability and insurance documentation. Submit the application to DAC at least 10 working days before first commercial activity.
required_dossiers: Application form for air freight broker/IAC status
Business plan covering charter brokerage activities
EU aviation security programme detailing screening of cargo and known consignor procedures
Certificate of insurance proving general liability and EU Regulation 785/2004 minimum insurance if any risk transfer to operator
RCS registration excerpt
Valid identity and good standing documents of managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DAC questions the security programme, supplement the programme within 15 days; an aggrieved applicant may file a recall or judicial appeal before the administrative courts within three months of a negative decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, Physical, and Occupational Premises Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); Commune (local municipal permits); Service d'Incendie et de Secours (SIC).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Secure a physical registered office and staff/work premises compliant with the Local Business Tax registration and municipal occupancy rules. Obtain building occupancy and fire safety attestations for the office floor, register the workplace with the municipal administration, and post the ITM workers' health and safety notice. If the SCSp later adds a bonded cargo warehouse, obtain a customs transit and customs storage license before operating the warehouse.
required_dossiers: Lease or ownership title for the registered office
Municipal building occupancy permit
Fire safety certificate from SIC
ITM workplace declaration
Customs warehouse authorization (only if warehousing cargo)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If municipal or fire authorities refuse the clearance, the company may correct the physical layout and re-submit; refusal decisions may be appealed in the administrative tribunal within three months. For customs warehouse, a corrective declaration can be filed with the Customs and Excise Administration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction de l'Aviation Civile (DAC) under the Ministry of Mobility and Public Works; European Commission and EASA for aviation safety rules.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Indirect Air Carrier (IAC) / Air Cargo Charter Broker Recognition under EU Regulation 2015/1998 (aviation security implementing rules) and Luxembourg national civil-aviation circulars; no EU air operator certificate (AOC) is required when the SCSp does not operate or lease aircraft with crew.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Category E – no full EIA for office-based cargo brokerage activities; registration and discharge permit only required if the SCSp undertakes dangerous-goods storage or physically handles cargo in a warehousing facility.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or emission thresholds apply to the office-only operation. Any domestic wastewater must be channelled to the municipal sewer network; all waste, including packaging, must be collected and treated by approved Luxembourg waste operators under the Luxembourg Waste Management Law and EU Waste Framework Directive.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Service d'Incendie et de Secours confirming the capacity and escape-plan compliance of the premises; municipal structural load and occupancy permit; ITM workplace health and safety clearance; an emergency plan and first-aid equipment must be maintained. If activity expands to a cargo terminal, additional structural load, dangerous goods segregation, and aviation security fence clearances must be obtained before operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for income/corporate taxes and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration formalities; unified online access via MyGuichet.lu, guichet.lu, and the ACD/AEDT taxpayer e-portals (eCDF / espace personnel).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Luxembourg SCSp is incorporated and filed with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) through a notary or via MyGuichet.lu; on RCS registration the competent authorities automatically assign the statutory matricule and a 13-digit Luxembourg VAT identification number (format LU + 7 digits + check digit). A foreign or non-established air-cargo charter broker without a Luxembourg fixed establishment must: (i) file the AEDT VAT application form through MyGuichet.lu; (ii) appoint a Luxembourg VAT agent when the AEDT requires a fiscal representative; (iii) furnish the constitutive documents, RCS excerpt (or foreign equivalent), and evidence of prospective taxable activity in Luxembourg; and (iv) obtain an EU EORI number from the Administration des douanes et accises for customs export procedures. Standard issuance timeline is approximately 10–15 working days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is fiscally transparent by default: income, gains, and net wealth are attributed directly to its partners, and the partnership is not independently subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax (IBT), or net wealth tax (NWT). The SCSp may, however, exercise the statutory election under Article 5bis of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR) to 'opt for taxation' and become an opaque entity fully subject to CIT, IBT, and NWT from the beginning of the relevant fiscal year. Hybrid mismatch rules (ATAD/ATAD II implemented by the law of 21 December 2017, as amended) may re-characterize or restrict deductions where the SCSp is treated as fiscally transparent in Luxembourg but opaque in a partner's jurisdiction, or vice versa.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration threshold exists for supplies of services or goods in Luxembourg: any taxable economic activity performed by a Luxembourg-established or non-established SCSp triggers mandatory VAT registration irrespective of turnover. For intra-EU distance sales of goods, the annual EUR 10,000 cross-border threshold applies; for non-established suppliers making taxable domestic supplies, VAT registration is required as of the first supply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently operate a real-time fiscal clearance (CTC) or transaction-level e-clearance regime. B2G e-invoicing is mandatory for suppliers delivering to public administrations under the EN 16931/PEPPOL framework since 2020. B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary; structured electronic formats, including hybrid and XML invoices, are administratively accepted. Luxembourg has announced alignment with the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) package and the successive introduction of mandatory B2B e-invoicing and digital transaction reporting in accordance with the EU-wide implementation timetable.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated treatment applies to (i) supplies of goods exported from Luxembourg to destinations outside the EU where shipment is evidenced by a valid customs export declaration; and (ii) services directly connected with international transport of goods, including international air-freight services and air-cargo charter brokerage (charter hire, cargo handling, and freight-forwarding services) for cargo dispatched to non-EU territory, provided the supplier retains contemporary documentary evidence of the transport chain, the services are rendered to a non-EU counterparty or to an EU forwarder for goods destined outside the EU, and the invoice contains the statutory export/international-transport zero-rating reference. The 0% rate is strictly conditional on proof of physical exportation or actual performance of the international transport service.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD / electronic AES export declaration sent to the Administration des douanes et accises)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill (AWB) evidencing dispatch from Luxembourg or another EU point to a non-EU destination
Inward Remittance Certificate / documentary proof of payment received from the foreign charterer, foreign broker, or non-EU consignee
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is strictly evidence-based. In a VAT audit, the AEDT may retroactively disallow the 0% rate and reassess output VAT at the standard 17% rate where the export or international-transport documentation is incomplete, inconsistent, or absent, with statutory late-payment interest accruing from the original due date. Administrative fines of up to EUR 25,000 per infraction may be imposed on the taxable person, with aggravated fines for recidivism. Intentional VAT or customs-export fraud gives rise to criminal prosecution, exposure to criminal fines and imprisonment under the Luxembourg VAT Law and the Luxembourg Criminal Code, publication of sanctions, and joint liability of the SCSp's general partner or managing partner for penalties arising from deliberate concealment or false documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for bank supervision and exchange control-related reporting; the BCL is also a member of the European System of Central Banks (ESCB).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a full member of the European Union and the euro area. The euro is fully convertible; capital movements, current payments, and profit remittances are generally unrestricted under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the EU Capital Movements Directive. No exchange control approvals are required for investment capital contributions, dividend/profit distributions, or trade-related cross-border payments. Profit remittance from a Luxembourg SCSp is subject only to standard withholding tax compliance, substance/economic reality review, and anti-money laundering / counter terrorist financing checks; legal convertibility barriers are effectively absent. However, transfers to or from high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions require enhanced due diligence, not exchange controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement or mandatory conversion ratio in Luxembourg. The euro being fully convertible, all export receipts in EUR or foreign currency may be retained, converted, or disbursed freely. A Luxembourg air cargo charter broker is not obliged to repatriate or sell export proceeds to the BCL or a licensed bank. Reporting obligations are limited to statistical balance-of-payments reporting thresholds and AML transaction monitoring/reporting by the banking counterparty.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) holding a valid Luxembourg or EU-passported licence under the EU E-Money Directive (Directive 2009/110/EC) and PSD2 are viable for limited-purpose receivables and disbursements, but they are not a full substitute for a commercial bank for capital escrow, commercial letters of credit, and large air-charter settlement operations. Off-shore or non-EU digital EMIs without a branch, agent, or passporting arrangement in Luxembourg are institutionally not viable for regulated corporate accounts; they cannot credibly provide the required AML/KYC, SWIFT correspondent relationships, and liquidity assurance for freight forwarding and charter brokerage transactions, and their use may trigger significant regulatory concern at the CSSF and BCL level.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), managing partner, or authorised signatory is generally required by Luxembourg AML/KYC practice under the Law of 12 November 2004, as amended, and CSSF prudential expectations. While identification and verification may be completed using remote onboarding tools supported by an EU qualified electronic signature and trusted eIDAS identity verification, banks retain discretion to require an in-person interview, notarised corporate documentation, and physical production of original passports. For a Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) with complex ownership, a physical or recorded management interview is highly likely to be mandated before account opening approval. Remote opening is permitted only where the bank's validated digital onboarding framework is used and where the SCSp documentation is fully certified; otherwise the default is physical presence for directors/managers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity and multi-layer corporate partnership structure of the SCSp
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current and certified Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) extract, annotated partnership agreement, deed of constitution, chain-of-ownership chart, and sworn declarations from ultimate natural persons; notarised copies of passports and proof of residence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction volumes and unusual payment flows from freight settlement activities, especially split payments, third-party chartered-in payments, or cash-clearance arrangements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full contract dossier: air charter agreements, bookings, invoices and settlement ledgers; commercial correspondence; Incoterms proof; transport documents (master air waybill, house air waybill, cargo manifests); and logical explanation for each round-trip or triangle flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags involving over/under-invoicing or double invoicing in air cargo charter brokerage
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent third-party valuation or broker commission schedule, actual charter contracts and slot/block-space agreements, aircraft registration certificates, fuel/handling fee invoices, and evidence of actual flight performance records from the aircraft operator.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and embargo exposure to airlines or jurisdictions on high-risk routes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated screening policy, real-time sanctions screening outputs, SICR disposition documentation, commodity/cargo classification per EU and UN sanctions regulations, OFAC and EU restrictive measures checks for each counterparty, and address/ownership breakdown for ultimate destination and end-user.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unregulated cross-border payments routed via private foreign bank accounts or unlicensed digital EMI
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements from approved licensed correspondent routes, SWIFT MT103 execution records, contractual assignment of payment rails, signed declarations that no anonymised or cryptocurrency-based settlement channels are used, and complete corporate treasury policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-transparent SCSp classification misuse for financing or money movements unrelated to commercial trade
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full partnership agreement and capital account statements, economic substance documentation (local office, directors, management accounts), transfer pricing analysis of brokerage margins, and proof that the SCSp is not used as a shell/conduit.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder or limited partner capital injections to the Luxembourg SCSp should be routed exclusively through regulated Tier-1 banks by SWIFT MT103 or equivalent bona fide wire instructions, using a clearly identified purpose code that describes the capital contribution to a partnership account, such as 'equity injection / capital contribution to partnership capital' in the underlying remittance information. The sending bank shall include a reference to the partnership agreement, the contributor's name, the source-of-funds proof, and the recipient's IBAN. For euro-denominated intra-EU injections, SEPA Credit Transfer is permissible; for USD or other non-EUR inflows, correspondents may require the use of an intermediary account. The bank must complete the beneficiary verification, and where applicable, provide BCL statistical reporting if the transaction reaches the relevant thresholds. No exchange control approval is required, but the moving bank should evidence the economic purpose of the injection to satisfy AML/KYC expectations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for air charter and freight forwarding settlements should use SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for straight payments to aircraft operators, airports, handlers, and suppliers; if the counterparty requires documentary security, eligible clearing rails include Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary credits subject to UCP 600) issued by the Luxembourg bank to the beneficiary bank. For euro payments inside the EEA, SEPA Credit Transfer is the primary clearing rail. For USD payments involving the United States, the payment should be cleared through the Correspondent account with Fedwire capability, while maintaining all sanctions screening and counterparty verification. The commercial freight ledger must aggregate each advance payment, contract invoice, and charter settlement in the same currency and with the funds flow corresponding to the underlying trade documents.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable foreign exchange forward contracts in EUR/USD and other liquid G10 currencies
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted-convertibility currencies where physical settlement is impossible, relying on a fix rate benchmark
Cross-currency swaps for converting and settling recurring USD-denominated charter payments versus EUR capital and operating accounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS declaration (declaration annuelle) confirming registered office, legal form, business object, general partner, managers and cessation status of the SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Societes, RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR); published data accessible via RESA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during 1-31 January; mandatory for all entities registered with the RCS as of 31 December of the preceding year; first declaration due in January following the SCSp incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing generates an RCS reminder letter; persistent default leads the Luxembourg district court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) to order deregistration (radiation d'office) with RESA publication; the general partner and managers face criminal fines of EUR 100 to EUR 2,500 per default under the Law of 19 December 2002, as amended

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit and publication of annual accounts (only if the SCSp qualifies as a large undertaking; below-threshold SCSps are exempt from filing and publication)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) / RESA (Recueil electronique des societes et associations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 31 July of the following year; partners' approval must occur within 6 months of year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deposit audited annual accounts exposes the general partner and managers to criminal fines of up to EUR 10,000 under the Law of 10 August 1915, as amended; repeated non-compliance allows the Public Prosecutor to petition for judicial dissolution or deregistration; the general partner carries civil liability for resulting damages

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO confirmation with the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs, RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), Ministry of Justice / Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during 1-30 September; confirmation certifies that the recorded UBO data (partners holding more than 25% or controlling the SCSp by other means) are accurate as at the confirmation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing, incomplete filing or false confirmation is punishable by criminal fines of EUR 125 to EUR 5,000 per breach under the Law of 13 January 2019, as amended; subsequent enforcement may include court-ordered deregistration of the SCSp

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual municipal business tax return (impot commercial communal, ICC) for the SCSp as a separate ICC taxpayer where it carries on a commercial or brokerage activity through a Luxembourg establishment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes, AED) via MyGuichet / eCDF electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually; for a 31 December year-end the AED-scheduled electronic filing deadline is 31 December of the following calendar year, unless the AED sets an earlier date on the tax return or through an official reminder
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission triggers the automatic 10% late-payment increase (droit en sus) on the assessed ICC plus monthly default interest at the statutory late-payment rate (0.6% per month); wilful omission constitutes tax fraud (fraude fiscale) punishable by fines of EUR 250 to EUR 12,500 and imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit and publication are triggered only when the SCSp is a large undertaking, i.e. it exceeds at least two of the following three criteria for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total EUR 20,000,000; net turnover EUR 40,000,000; average workforce of 250 employees. Below these thresholds the SCSp is exempt from statutory audit, annual accounts filing and RESA publication; the partnership agreement may nevertheless require a voluntary audit or an agreed-upon-procedures engagement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts and the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended; EU-adopted IFRS may be applied where the partnership agreement so provides; accounting records must be suitable for allocating the SCSp's taxable results to the partners under the pass-through regime.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner must file with the RBE any rectification arising from a transfer of partnership interests revealing a new beneficial owner (any natural person holding or controlling more than 25%) before the annual confirmation; the mandatory annual confirmation is due in September and certifies that the RBE data are complete, accurate and up to date; the register is electronic and supported by a physical KYC file kept at the registered office or with the professional fiduciary, refreshed upon any material ownership change or at the frequency required by the SCSp's AML risk assessment.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of partners (record of general and limited partners, capital contributions, assignment and transfer history of partnership interests)
Minute book of partners' meetings and general partner resolutions (including written consents and formal management decisions)
Beneficial owner register file (UBO identification, ownership percentages, control details, and underlying KYC documentation)
Register of the general partner and managers (appointment acts, removal, powers of representation, and identity of legal representatives)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 18,000 - 45,000 when the large-undertaking audit threshold is exceeded; contractual review engagements, if required by the partnership agreement or financiers, typically range from 6,000 to 15,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City combined rate: 17% corporate income tax + 7% unemployment fund surcharge on the CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax; rates applicable to tax years 2024-2025)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box regime: 80% exemption on net qualifying IP income, yielding an effective rate of approximately 4.99%; investment tax credits for digitalisation (12%) and environmental assets (20%); participation exemption for qualifying shareholdings (10% shareholding or EUR 6,000,000 acquisition cost held 12 months). For a fiscally transparent SCSp, the entity itself bears no CIT; profits pass through pro rata to partners, who apply the abovementioned incentives at their own level.
